agent.howItWorksBody: The {{name}} agent is a small daemon that runs on the host and forwards local events to UTMStack over an authenticated TLS connection. It auto-updates and reports its health.
agent.installHint: Run this command on every {{name}} host you want to monitor. The token already encodes your current workspace.
agent.after1: The host appears under Data Sources within ~60 seconds of agent start.
agent.after2: Telemetry begins flowing into Log Explorer, scoped to your workspace.
agent.after3: The agent self-reports CPU / memory / disk health back to UTMStack.

collector.howItWorksBody: {{name}} doesn't run a UTMStack agent. Instead, you install the UTMStack collector somewhere on the network that both your {{name}} device and UTMStack can reach. {{name}} sends syslog to the collector, the collector parses, normalizes, and forwards events into UTMStack.
collector.step1Hint: Run on a Linux host with network access from the {{name}} device.
collector.step2Hint: On the {{name}} device, point syslog forwarding to the collector's address on {{port}}.
collector.step3Body: Within a few minutes you should see {{name}} events under source: {{source}} in Log Explorer, and a new entry in Data Sources.

cloud.howItWorksBody: {{name}} runs entirely inside UTMStack — no agent or collector to deploy. Provide read-only API credentials and UTMStack will pull events on a schedule, parse them, and ingest them into Log Explorer.
cloud.after1: UTMStack performs an initial backfill of recent events.
cloud.after2: From then on, events are pulled every 1–5 minutes (depends on the API).
cloud.after3: The integration appears under Data Sources with current pull status and lag.

custom.whenBody: When your source isn't in the catalog. Forward arbitrary syslog or JSON to UTMStack and define a parser to normalize fields.
custom.parserBody: UTMStack will auto-detect JSON keys and propose field mappings. You can override mappings in the parser editor and add Grok patterns for free-form text.
